failure_patterns.pattern: strength_mismatch: Answers either added unsupported refinements to a valid core claim or gave only one direction of the requested criterion.

rejected_edits.content:
## Compound-option and referent audit
- Decompose each option into its core claim and every added modifier or conjunct. Verify each clause independently: support for a basis, period inclusion, or other core result does not establish extra closure, finite generation, structural properties, invariance, or a sharper classification. One unsupported clause invalidates the whole option.
- Conversely, when asked for the strongest claim or a complete criterion, do not stop at a sufficient direction if the result also establishes the converse. For exact classifications, check both the claimed members and that no others qualify; uniqueness does not imply invariance under rescaling.
- Keep the referent fixed. A property proved for a decorated, conditioned, or otherwise modified object does not automatically hold for the underlying object, and a claim on a restricted parameter set does not automatically extend beyond it.

- For piecewise classifications, audit branch conditions separately from branch expressions: check exact endpoints and strict versus inclusive comparisons, ensure the branches cover the allowed domain, handle overlaps, and verify every branch including “otherwise.”
- For uniform estimates, track the full parameter range and which variables the constants may depend on; do not silently turn a parameter-dependent estimate into a uniform one.
- When a conclusion concerns a limit, check whether the asserted property is preserved under the stated convergence; convergence of the underlying objects or parameters alone does not guarantee it.
